content: Aztreonam is a medication used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It is typically administered by injection into a vein or muscle as directed by your doctor. Before using, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration; do not use the liquid if either is present. For optimal effectiveness, use this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache, blurred vision, or redness, discomfort, pain, or swelling at the injection site. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush, a new vaginal yeast infection, or a new bacterial infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Before using aztreonam, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, or to penicillins, cephalosporins, or other antibiotics such as imipenem or meropenem, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Aztreonam may rarely cause dizziness, and alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks requiring alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication may reduce the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, aztreonam should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Aztreonam may interfere with certain lab tests, such as some diabetic urine tests, potentially causing false results. If someone overdoses and experiences serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. Lab and medical tests may be conducted while you are using this medication. Keep all medical and lab appointments. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, consult the product instructions and your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
